statFormula.namedHuman: attack + health = 2 * cost + 1. Named Humans are the Bible characters (the h_ ids in CardLibrary.swift), as opposed to the generic archetypes. The premium is exactly +1, never more. Named Creatures get no premium.
statFormula.creature: attack + health = 2 * cost - 1, minimum 2. The minimum exists because a cost-1 Creature would otherwise be 1/0 (dead on arrival) or 0/1 (unable to attack).
statFormula.exceptions: Leviathan (15, formula says 13) and Lamb (3, formula says 2) are deliberate exceptions. Leave them alone.

vocabulary.creature: Always capitalized; always means the card type. A Human in the Frontier is not a Creature and cannot be targeted by Creature-targeting text.
vocabulary.defend: Your card is the one being attacked.
vocabulary.blocking: Does not exist in this game. Neither does 'fighting'.
vocabulary.damaged: Current Health is below max Health.
vocabulary.lowestHealth: How 'weakest' is measured. Ties break by board order.
vocabulary.overnight: A card has spent the night once it has been in play throughout the opponent's entire turn.
vocabulary.heal: Only two forms: 'Heal N' and 'Heal to full'.
vocabulary.scopeDefault: An effect that names no side refers to your own cards. Text says 'enemy' when it means the opponent's. Condition checks may still read 'if you control ...'.
vocabulary.points: A Creature's own point value is a printed stat — its element value 1-3, written beside the Element as '2 Sea'. Only cards that MODIFY someone else's points use text, and it is written '+N <Element> points' or as a multiplier (Moses, Fish Net).

definitions.charge: May March the same turn it's played, skipping the overnight wait.
definitions.shield: Prevents the first instance of combat damage this card would take each turn. A printed Shield refreshes at the start of its controller's turn. A granted Shield lasts only for the duration the granting card states.
definitions.guard: This card's ability is active only while it is in your Basecamp. It switches off the moment the card Marches, dies, or otherwise leaves.

notes.blessing: Not a keyword. When a Creature's Sacrifice ability buffs a Human, it's called a Blessing.
notes.guardian: Not a card keyword. See rules.basecampGuardian.

deckConstruction.effect: A deck is 28 bodies (Humans and Creatures) and must contain at least 2 cards costing 1, so the preparing phase can always seed a Basecamp.
deckConstruction.relics: The 2 Relics are chosen separately and are NOT part of the 28. They begin the game face-down in the Relic slots.

preparingPhase.effect: Before turn 1: flip a coin for who goes first, then seed each Basecamp with 2 of that player's own cost-1 deck cards (chosen at random, flipped face-up) while the deck is still untouched, then deal opening hands (3 to the first player, 4 to the second — the extra card offsets going first). Seeding runs before dealing specifically so it always has the full deck's cost-1 cards available. No card is converted to mana during preparing. None of this is a player choice.
preparingPhase.guardian: The two seeded cards are placed in Basecamp order at random, so which one lands in slot 1 (the Guardian) is also random.
preparingPhase.firstPlayer: The coin flip happens first, before hands are dealt, so the draw can compensate for it. Nothing currently compensates further into the game — going first still has a Mana Pool tempo edge past turn 1.

mana.zone: Mana Pool — sits beside the hand. Every card in it is worth 1 mana.
mana.convertEffect: Once per turn you may convert a card from hand to your Mana Pool. Its mana is available the same turn you convert it. Converting is optional, but skipping it leaves you permanently a mana behind.
mana.permanence: Cards in the Mana Pool are there permanently. They never return to hand, deck or discard, and the card's own text does nothing while it is mana — only its existence counts. The Mana Pool is NOT the discard, so discard recursion (River Otter) cannot recover converted cards.
mana.refill: At the start of each of your turns your mana refills to the size of your Mana Pool.
mana.atCap: At 10 cards the Pool is full and you can no longer convert.
mana.curve: The Pool starts empty — 0 mana on turn 1. Nothing is converted during preparing.

rules.basecampGuardian: Basecamp slots are numbered 1-4 in the order cards are placed. The card in slot 1 is the Guardian and takes all incoming Raid damage. When the Guardian dies or leaves the Basecamp, every other card shifts up one slot, and whichever card is now in slot 1 becomes the new Guardian.
rules.frontierOverflow: If the Frontier is at its 5-card max, a player can discard a card or Sacrifice a Creature to make room.
rules.marchRule: A card must have spent the night in its zone before it can March, unless it has Charge.
rules.combat: When a card attacks from the Frontier, the attacker and the defender each deal damage equal to their Attack to the other. A card whose Health reaches 0 goes to the discard.
rules.raid: If the opponent's Frontier is empty, an attacker hits the opponent's Basecamp Guardian instead. A Raid takes no retaliation.
rules.altar: Sacrificed Creatures go to the Altar. Clearing an Event flushes your Altar to the discard. Cards that die in combat go straight to the discard, not the Altar.
rules.sacrificeBaseline: Every Creature prints an element value from 1 to 3 beside its Element (e.g. '2 Sea'). Sacrificing it moves it to the Altar and gives that many points of its Element. The element value is a printed stat like Attack and Health, not ability text, and needs no trigger written on the card.
rules.elementValuesPending: The 1-3 element values are NOT yet assigned on any Creature card. They are being set separately. Minnow Shoal, Kraken and Ant currently encode their value in ability text ('+2 Sea points', '+3 Sea points', '+2 Land points'); that text must be deleted when printed values land, or those cards will double-count.
rules.pointModifierOrder: 1) Set the base amount (the Creature's printed element value). 2) Apply flat modifiers (Moses). 3) Apply multipliers (Fish Net). A Creature printing '3 Sea' with Moses and Fish Net = (3 + 1) * 2 = 8 Sea points.
rules.relics: Each deck chooses 2 Relics. They are not part of the 28-card deck and are never played from hand. They begin face-down in the 2 Relic slots and cost no mana. Clearing Event 1 flips one Relic face-up (the player's choice which); clearing Event 2 flips the other; clearing Event 3 wins the game and grants nothing. A face-down Relic does nothing; once flipped it is permanent and its text is live. A cascading clear flips one Relic per Event cleared. Relic cards still carry a printed cost — it is UNUSED under these rules and is retained only pending a decision on whether to repurpose it.
rules.eventStructure: Each player has their own Event 1 and Event 2; Event 3 is shared. Events unlock one at a time: only Event 1 is face-up at the start, clearing it reveals Event 2, and clearing Event 2 unlocks Event 3. When either player unlocks Event 3 it is revealed to both, but a player who has not cleared their own Events 1 and 2 can see it without being able to clear it.
rules.eventClearing: Clearing an Event subtracts exactly its requirement — any surplus stays banked — flushes your Altar, and flips one of your face-down Relics (see rules.relics). Clears cascade: if clearing Event 1 leaves enough points for the Event 2 it just revealed, that clears too, in the same action, flipping a second Relic.
rules.winCondition: First player to overcome all 3 of their Events reaches the Promised Land and wins.
rules.loseCondition: A player loses when their Basecamp is emptied BY COMBAT. You may never voluntarily empty it — the last Basecamp card cannot March or be Sacrificed.
